chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who has children from a mother other than the primary one (or from different mothers), should he prefer some of them over others? He said, 'There is no harm in doing so.'

Hariz said: Muawiya and Abu Kahmas informed me that they heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him) did that with his son al-Hasan, and al-Husayn did that with his son Ali, and my father did that with me, and I did it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible
key_terms.يُفَضِّلُ: to prefer or give preference to

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a father to give more to one child than another in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of preferential bequest (*tarjih*) among children from different mothers, a ruling supported by the continuous practice (*athar*) of the Ahl al-Bayt. By citing Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and the Imams themselves, the text underscores that this was not an isolated legal opinion but a established familial tradition, reinforcing the authority of the Imams in personal law. This practice highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding inheritance distribution outside of the fixed Quranic shares.
